correctness.rationale: The outside cell (a,b) has d_H(a)+d_H(b) neighbors, reducing fort status exactly to incompatibility of zero-degree and degree-one vertices in opposite root partitions. Inclusion-minimality by cases: full cover yields spanning star forests with one-sided exception; one-side uncovered forces degree-2 covered vertices and acyclic contracted multigraph or single cycle; both sides uncovered force a single proper even cycle. Cayley labeled trees, alternating cycles, and corrected star EGF yield Q. Independent direct neighborhood and all-proper-subset test for (2,5),(2,6),(3,3),(3,4) found respectively {4:100,5:10}, {4:225,6:12}, {3:6,4:18}, {4:54,5:12,6:24}, matching independent coefficient claims. The complete arbitrary board result depends on structural proof, not those checks.

value.rationale: The naturally defined minimal-fort antichain controls zero-forcing obstructions; exact structural three-class census and nontrivial missing-size intervals on thin rook boards are useful combinatorial invariants not recovered from a generic product inequality.

final_claim: For every m,n>=2, inclusion-minimal forts in rook graph K_m□K_n are precisely corrected spanning star forests, one-sided degree-two contracted forests, or proper alternating cycles; explicit bivariate labeled EGF Q and two-row polynomial with missing cardinalities.
limitations: The finite board test does not prove full m,n; relied on case proof and formal labeled generating function.
Absolute novelty could depend on unindexed line-graph/fort census literature.
